activities.anchor: Two rules govern every one of them
activities.caption: file each process by which rule it obeys
activities.name: ecoRulesBuckets

config.prompt: Matter cycles; energy flows — file each traffic flow:

items.label: carbon passing from soil to plant to animal and back
nitrogen recycling between air, soil and bodies
water through an organism back to the sky
sunlight captured, then leaked away as heat at every step

config.why: Two genuinely different behaviours: matter recirculates like water in a sealed pipe network; energy moves like a conveyor that only travels upward and bleeds at every station.

activities.caption: call the capture — the sunlight gateway
activities.name: ecoGatewayEstimate

config.prompt: Of all the solar energy striking a leaf, roughly what fraction ends up captured in sugars?
config.why: About 1% — the rest is reflected, transmitted, or spent warming and cooling the plant.
config.context: Which is why the whole trophic pyramid is built on a trickle worth counting carefully.

activities.anchor: grew a willow for five years in about
activities.caption: bet before you read on — where a tree's mass comes from
activities.name: ecoWillowPredict

config.q: Van Helmont grew a willow for five years in about 90 kg of soil, and the tree gained about 74 kg. Where did the new mass come from?
choices: Mostly from the soil it stood in
Mostly from carbon dioxide pulled from the air and water drawn from the ground
From the minerals in the fertiliser
config.why: The soil lost barely 60 grams. Nearly all dry biomass is built from air and water; soil supplies only small quantities of minerals.

activities.caption: pair each role with its place in the pipeline
activities.name: ecoRolesMatch

config.prompt: The feeding steps, named and placed — pair them:

pairs.right: bacteria and fungi recycling dead matter
earthworms and woodlice, feeding on dead matter

config.why: The recycling crew runs off to the side of the chain, returning molecules to the soil while energy climbs one way only.

activities.anchor: The physics behind this is not negotiable
activities.caption: find the faulty line — where the 90% goes
activities.name: ecoLossSpot

config.prompt: A student explains the trophic losses — one line is faulty, click it:
lines: Energy is never created or destroyed, only changed in form — the first law.
Every conversion degrades some of it to heat that disperses — the second law.
So the 90% lost at each step loops back to the producers as usable energy.
Indigestible parts — cellulose, bone, hide — lock energy away from the eater.
A large share passes sideways to the decomposers.
config.correction: The dispersed heat can never be gathered to power anything — it does not loop back; an ecosystem needs a continuous input of sunlight or it stops.
config.why: Biology cannot repeal either law; it can only live inside them — open for energy, effectively closed for matter.

activities.anchor: Ecologists keep two ledgers at the pipeline's base
activities.caption: fill the blanks — gross vs net
activities.name: ecoLedgerCloze

config.text: Gross primary productivity is the total energy producers fix by %%0%%. Net primary productivity is what remains after the producers pay their own %%1%% — the actual surplus every other level lives on. In the classic Silver Springs study, producers captured 20,810 kilocalories per square metre per year, but nearly %%2%% of that was spent running the plants themselves.
config.hint: Plants are not charities — the distinction matters because growth happens only while photosynthesis out-earns respiration.

activities.anchor: The trophic handoffs have been measured, not just modelled
activities.caption: stack Odum's Silver Springs audit
activities.name: ecoAuditOrder

config.prompt: Howard Odum's measured audit — stack the receipts, largest first:
items: Producers fixed 20,810 kcal per m² per year
Herbivores received 3,368 — about 16%, a generous pipeline
config.why: Decomposers processed 5,060 — more than the herbivores: the 'invisible' end of the pipeline handles the bulk of the flow.

activities.anchor: Forests are the planet's great energy collectors
activities.caption: two strategies, one sunlight — drag between them
activities.name: ecoForestCompare

config.prompt: Three designs for the same job — two shown, drag the divider:

before.label: tropical rainforest
before.text: The skyscraper: layered canopy, over half of all land species, wealth in the living biomass — cleared, it turns to hardpan within seasons, because the fertility was the forest, not the dirt.

after.label: boreal forest (taiga)
after.text: Cold and slow: evergreen needles for a running start, acidic litter slowing decay, fungi doing the work cold bacteria cannot — the most carbon-hoarding of the three.

config.why: Temperate deciduous splits the difference: dropped leaves build rich brown soils, fewer species but larger standing biomass per species.
